six cases of RMSF in persons with exposure in Tecate, Mexico were reported to the California Department of Public Health; three patients died.
Six cases of RMSF caused by Rickettsia rickettsii , including three deaths, were reported to the California Department of Public Health during July 2023–January 2024.
The identification of six confirmed cases of RMSF in southern California over 6 months is unusual

public_health_question.v: What were the clinical course, diagnosis and exposure source of a cluster of severe and fatal RMSF cases reported in California after exposure in Tecate, Mexico?

ev.q: All six patients were eventually determined to have had exposure to R. rickettsii in Tecate, Mexico
Severe and Fatal Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever After Exposure in Tecate, Mexico — California, July 2023–January 2024

ev.q: The six RMSF patients ranged in age from 17 months to 65 years, and all but one were male

notes: The Discussion sets the six cases in 6 months beside a cited average of one confirmed case per year in California (2011–2019); this is a cited baseline, so the record is treated as a descriptive case series (limited). Prepass cues for weighting (diffusion-weighted imaging) and diagnostic accuracy (cited sensitivity of molecular tests) are false hits.
